text:
Patrick Kane came home to Chicago, and the homecoming has been mostly frustration so far. He has one goal in 15 games and none in his last 14, and the Blackhawks have been buried at five on five with him on the ice (35% of the expected goals). Then came a stint on injured reserve; Jeff Blashill has since called him day to day.

Some of this is bad luck. He's had 3.1 expected goals and scored once, and Chicago has scored 7.6 fewer goals than expected with him out there, the kind of gap that usually closes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still sees the old Kane in the details: a setup man in the 95th percentile for primary shot assists, with 55% of his shots off the rush.

He's 37, with three Cups, a Hart and an Art Ross behind him and 1,400 career points coming in. Our range for his season is 46 to 70 points. The goals should come. Whether they come fast enough to matter for this team is another question.
